don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

* don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests

Also applies the same treatment to the string index mapping table,
which was sized from the string count before the RLE ranges were read:
build both as the data is actually parsed and validate string indices
against the mapping entries that were provided. Well-formed manifests
whose RLE ranges cover every string are unaffected.

* modify _manifest in place to avoid chance of unnecessary copy

---------

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Two independent checks are added, since either alone leaves the other
failure mode reachable:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value. This does
  *not* impose an absolute size ceiling: OpenEXR places no fixed limit
  on data size by default (see `Header::setMaxImageSize()`, which is
  off/unlimited unless an application opts in), so a legitimate manifest
  may be arbitrarily large provided the file actually contains that much
  compressed data.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, exactly as the adjacent
  `readStringList()` already does for its own reads. This is the fix
  that actually matters for the null/overread cases, since `init()` is
  reachable directly through the public `IDManifest(const char*, const
  char*)` constructor without ever passing through the size check above.

While adding these, hoist the string table size into a local in
`init()` and use it for the string table bounds checks there instead
of recomputing `stringList.size()` at each site.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

Verified by regenerating the reporter's PoC files (declared sizes of
512 MiB, 0, and 1) against `exrmanifest`: all are now rejected with a
clean exception instead of crashing or being killed by the OOM killer.
Also verified that a legitimate, honestly-compressed 300 MB manifest is
still accepted. The existing `testIDManifest` suite, which round-trips
legitimate manifests up to ~44 MB decoded, continues to pass.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Sonnet 5)

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

coupling:
Both edited commits touch IDManifest::init() in src/lib/OpenEXR/ImfIDManifest.cpp, the parser for the serialized idManifest attribute, reached through the public Imf::IDManifest(const char*, const char*) constructor.

Commit d6f75dc4 ("don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests") converts the string-index mapping table from a vector<int> preallocated to stringList.size() (filled via a running currentIndex cursor) into a table grown with push_back as the RLE mapping ranges are actually read. That change alone is safe, and the commit is benign on its own: within the same diff it re-bounds the downstream consumer, validating each compressed-ID table entry's stringIndex against mapping.size() (the number of mapping entries actually provided) instead of stringList.size().

Commit 38d9cbf4 ("Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read") is a bounds-hardening commit; its added hunks gate the version-field read and the compressed-manifest expansion ratio. Its cleanup hunk hoists stringList.size() into a local numStrings and mechanically replaces every remaining stringList.size() use in init() -- including the guard d6f75dc4 had re-bound to mapping.size() -- with numStrings, i.e. the string-table size. Read in its own world (where mapping is still preallocated to stringList.size()) that substitution is a literal no-op: mapping.size() == stringList.size() always holds, so this commit is a pure, behavior-preserving cleanup.

Only when the two compose does the invariant break: mapping may now legitimately be shorter than the string list (well-formed manifests need not cover every string with an RLE range), so validating a table entry's stringIndex against numStrings no longer bounds the following mapping[stringIndex] access. A crafted manifest whose RLE ranges provide fewer mapping entries than a table entry's string index references reads past the end of the mapping allocation (heap-buffer-overflow read of 4 bytes at stringList[mapping[stringIndex]], ImfIDManifest.cpp:585 on the resulting tree).

The defect is visible in neither diff alone: d6f75dc4's diff is self-consistently safe (the index is re-bounded to mapping.size() inside the same commit), and 38d9cbf4's guard substitution only changes behavior if mapping.size() can differ from stringList.size() -- knowledge that exists only in d6f75dc4's diff. A correct fix must reason across both commits: reverting 38d9cbf4's substitution hunk restores a correct guard, but that hunk is a provable no-op within 38d9cbf4's own context, so justifying it requires reading d6f75dc4; conversely 'fixing' d6f75dc4 (returning to preallocation) changes code that is correct as written once 38d9cbf4's hoist is in place. Neither commit's diff, inspected in isolation, contains an unchecked access; the unchecked access exists only on the composition, which is what makes the case delocalized.

pocs.entry_point: Imf::IDManifest(const char* data, const char* end) (public constructor declared in ImfIDManifest.h); the probe feeds a crafted serialized idManifest blob to it
